_comment: Alert rules for south, the management plane. Applied to Grafana's unified alerting via
Four rules, and the list is deliberately short. Every one of them corresponds to something
that actually had to be discovered by hand on 2026-08-22; an alert nobody would act on is
worse than no alert, because it teaches people to ignore the channel.
NoDataState is 'Alerting' on purpose throughout. Absence of data is the failure mode this
estate is most exposed to — a dead collector, a dead host and a rejected write all look
identical from here, and treating silence as health is how a broken thing gets recorded as
fine. It will occasionally page for a Grafana-side problem. That is the right trade.

annotations.description: Either the host is down, the collector has stopped, or writes are being rejected. These are indistinguishable from here — check the host directly before concluding anything, and remember that AWX runs on this plane, so an objective that tries to diagnose it may itself be affected.
annotations.runbook: ssh to the host; systemctl is-active alloy; then AWX [67] General: Machines: Check kernel health

annotations.description: On the PostgreSQL VM this matters more than it looks: AWX stores everything in that database, and a full disk degrades AWX in ways that present as AWX being broken rather than as a disk problem.
MemAvailable rather than free: free memory is meaningless on a host with a healthy page cache, and alerting on it produces noise that gets the channel muted.

annotations.summary: {{ $labels.instance }} is losing over 5% of CPU to steal
annotations.description: The hypervisor is oversubscribed. NOTE: this is NOT the soft-lockup fault seen on west on 2026-08-22 — steal was near zero on hosts that were locking up hard, so a quiet version of this alert rules nothing out. Soft lockups are only visible on the host, via AWX [67] Check kernel health.
annotations.runbook: AWX [67] General: Machines: Check kernel health
